doc.title: Jake Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997

title: Ted Weems and Buddy Morrow bands
summary: Weems was his first big band; Buddy Morrow's rhythm-and-blues-flavored band was very good.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel

blocks.x: Well we were talking about actually how you got started with big bands, but Woody Herman was your first big band?

No Ted Weems was my first big band, yeah, Ted Weems was. And then I played in a very good band after that, Buddy Morrow had a very good band when I worked with them, it was way better than Woody’s band that he had at the time, very good. Kenny Peplowski worked with Buddy. And he said the same thing. He says he’s a great guy to work with and always had a good band. But the band I was with was Dave on piano and Dick Johnson on alto, and Ray Diceo, and Rick Davis, a very good tenor player. We had a very good band, a very good band. And we played rhythm & blues both, oh I forget what the tune, “Night Train” naturally, that was his most famous record. And a lot of other tunes, “Red Top” and things like that. But the big band arrangements, they were fun to play, fun to play.
